S/4HANA assessment expertise

KaarTech has completed 15+ S/4HANA assessments across the USA, Europe and the Middle East, including Willscott, Riddell, Dole and Motiva. Each one is system-driven, using KTern.AI to analyze the ECC landscape, then validated with process owners in structured workshops. The outputs form one connected plan: platform and deployment model, migration approach, business case, licensing and five-year TCO, a phased and costed roadmap, and the program organization to deliver it.

The same teams also deliver ECC to S/4HANA transformations, so every recommendation draws on delivery experience. Phase 0 is an investment: it sizes scope correctly, settles major decisions early and surfaces data, integration and readiness gaps before they reach the timeline. The deliverables belong to SLOAN and carry into implementation regardless of the system integrator chosen.

Our understanding of SLOAN

A manufacturer since 1906, with a deadline on December 31, 2028

SLOAN designs and manufactures commercial restroom and water-management products: flushometers, toilets, urinals, faucets, sinks, soap dispensers and connected fixtures. It is a recognised voice in water conservation and sustainable building design, focused on the United States with a growing global presence.

With repetitive and configure-to-order lines serving distributors, contractors, engineers and specifiers, SLOAN depends on tight integration between sales, engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, finance and customer service. Its ECC landscape has grown through enhancements, custom developments and interfaces to surrounding applications.

The dates that frame every option

External dates

ECC mainstream maintenance ends 2027, extended to 2030. CPI Neo shuts down December 31, 2028.

Clean Core ambition

Move to Clean Core on-prem or on RISE, and modernize where it creates value without adding scope or risk to the migration.

Operational reality

Repetitive and configure-to-order manufacturing, with variant configuration, rebates and a third-party packing and shipping solution at the main plant.

Limited bandwidth

A strong in-house SAP team with deep process knowledge but limited capacity, and heavy reliance on key SMEs.

SLOAN's draft BTP direction

  • S/4HANA as system of record, with SAP BTP carrying four pillars: Integration, Extension, Data and AI.
  • Integration Suite replaces CPI on Neo. iFlows are rebuilt to current needs, not lifted and shifted, and duplicate tenants are rationalized.
  • Extension through SAP Build Process Automation, Build Work Zone and Document AI, side by side and Clean Core aligned.
  • Two Neo exit sequences: progressive migration before cutover, or re-platforming together at cutover.

SLOAN's draft analytics direction

  • One system of record, one enterprise data platform with a single semantic layer, one enterprise BI layer.
  • BW and BusinessObjects retire after S/4HANA is stable, not inside the cutover.
  • Option A: Embedded Analytics, Databricks and Power BI. Option B: A plus SAC for integrated planning. Option C: Business Data Cloud / Datasphere with SAC.
  • Open questions: integrated financial planning, Business Data Cloud maturity, and the future of Insight Software.

What SLOAN wants from this program

    SLOAN wants a decision-ready, SLOAN-specific recommendation rather than generic S/4HANA benefits. Our response treats the draft architecture positions as proposals to validate, refine or challenge with evidence, and uses KTern.AI analysis of the ECC system to ground that challenge in how SLOAN's processes, custom code and interfaces actually run.

        Options analysis and decision method

        One method is used for platform and deployment, migration approach and phasing, so results are comparable.

        Agree first.Criteria, weights and pass/fail conditions are agreed with leadership before any option is scored.
        Screen, then score.Options failing a mandatory condition drop out. The rest are scored 1–5 against written anchors, with evidence.
        Test the result.Weight sensitivity shows whether a different weighting would change the recommendation.
        Decide together.Pre-scores are refined with SLOAN in decision workshops. The recommendation says when another option would be preferred.
        Record.Every decision goes in the decision log with rationale, owner and date. SLOAN keeps the log.

        Roadmap method

        Fixed constraints firstECC maintenance dates, the Neo shutdown, the draft Q2 2027–Q3 2028 window and SLOAN's business calendar come before any scenario.
        Built from the decisionsPlatform (Obj. 1) and approach (Obj. 2) shape two or three phasing options (Obj. 4), each with benefit timing (Obj. 3), cost (Obj. 6) and pre-projects (Obj. 5).
        Tested for realismDecision gates, a contingency plan and a P50/P80 go-live date per option show the risk of slipping past Neo.
        Ready to act onAn owner, entry criteria and latest start date for each step, as the basis for implementation partner selection.
        KTern.AI, the evidence engine

        One read-only analysis of ECC feeds all seven objectives

        KaarTech starts from system evidence, not questionnaires. KTern.AI is SAP-certified and listed in SAP Store. It connects read-only through the standard SAP RFC protocol, with no add-ons or plugins installed on ECC, and produces first results within 3–5 business days of connection. The connectivity is validated and listed by SAP in the SAP API Business Hub.

        Frameworks that extend the assessment beyond the brief

        SAP Signavio Process Insights, Discovery Edition

        An optional service for an initial read on process performance from SLOAN's existing SAP data: three predefined process flows with indicators, root causes, bottlenecks and estimated monetary benefit.

        1Technical preparation. Guide SLOAN's team through SAP Notes 2745851 and 2758146 and the data extraction.
        2Data submission. Review the ZIP file. SLOAN completes the request form and upload itself, as SAP does not allow partners to submit for customers.
        3Tenant provisioning. Support access to the Discovery Edition tenant.
        4Insights review. Interpret indicators, bottlenecks and SAP's recommendations.

        KaarTech Business Value Realization framework

        Built into Phase 0 to set a baseline and connect priorities, current-state challenges and improvements to measurable outcomes.

        1Discover value drivers in Value Discovery Workshops, structured with the APQC PCF.
        2Establish the baseline: current performance, KPIs and measurable targets by function.
        3Define value opportunities, separating S/4HANA-driven gains from other initiatives and naming owners.
        4Enable value tracking through a Business Transformation Cockpit.

        Enterprise architecture and application rationalization

        Visibility into the current IT landscape, its dependencies and gaps, and a future-state architecture aligned with the S/4HANA transformation.

        • Discovery: baseline of business capabilities, applications, data platforms, technology and integration.
        • Mapping and dependency analysis: applications to capabilities, processes, interfaces and technology.
        • Fit and rationalization: business value, functional fit, technical health, lifecycle and integration complexity, to retain, replace, consolidate or retire.
        • Target state and roadmap: future architecture, transition dependencies and a phased plan.

        Risk management approach

        Assumptions, changes and risks are managed in the open

        Assumption management

        Estimates and recommendations depend on assumptions about scope, data, third-party systems and SAP commercial terms.

        1Log. Every assumption goes in the KTern.AI register with source, owner (SLOAN or KaarTech), affected deliverable and validation date.
        2Validate. Confirm in workshops, from system data or through SLOAN's single point of contact, and review in the weekly status meeting.
        3Close or convert. A confirmed assumption becomes a fact or decision. A wrong one is raised as a risk, or as a change if it affects scope or schedule.

        Change control

        Any deviation from the agreed scope is a Change Order, estimated and mutually agreed before work begins.

        • Change Control Board: executives from SLOAN and KaarTech, confirmed at kickoff, assess impact and approve either way.
        • Change Order Form: every change is raised with a unique ID.
        • Change Order Tracker: one place to register, monitor, control and close changes, kept by the Engagement Lead.

        Risks by objective

        Each objective carries its own risk and mitigation table in the objectives explorer. The patterns repeat:

        • Criteria or evidence agreed late, so agree and approve first.
        • Thin SME capacity, so ring-fence roles and schedule focused sessions.
        • Opinion standing in for evidence, so record source and confidence.
        • Dates assumed, not tested, so model critical paths and show P50/P80.
        • Perceived bias toward SAP or KaarTech, so disclose, and score only on SLOAN-approved criteria.
